svg.title: Navier-Stokes critical frontier — Batch-3 review candidate
svg.desc: A quantitative status ladder separates the scaling-critical line, conditional continuation criteria, partial regularity, and the still-open universal three-dimensional smoothness or breakdown alternative.
svg.text: The regularity frontier is a hierarchy of conditional statements
Scaling, continuation criteria, partial regularity, and the open global question must not be collapsed into one frontier icon.
Criticality marks scale invariance of the norm; it is not itself a regularity theorem.
If a controlling critical norm stays finite on [0,T), the strong solution extends beyond T.
Suitable weak solutions have a quantitatively small possible singular set; the theorem does not prove that the set is empty.
For every admissible smooth datum: prove global smoothness, or construct a valid finite-time breakdown example in an official setting.
A sufficient continuation hypothesis is not known to hold universally.
Do not infer the endpoint from the ladder
Energy control, conditional continuation, and partial regularity are genuine theorems; together they still do not settle the Clay alternative.
Review candidate · documentary exposition only · visual_is_evidence: false
